title: [Full Workshop] Building Conversational AI Agents - Thor Schaeff, ElevenLabs
talk_summary: This is a hands-on ElevenLabs workshop on building multilingual voice agents: ASR → LLM → streaming TTS, with dashboard/API/MCP configuration, language-detection system tools, per-language voice assignment, and agent-to-agent transfers. It is almost entirely product demo and audience Q&A about voice latency, pricing, and accents, with no engineering practices for agent orchestration, review, or cost control.

takeaways.technique: Silent agent-to-agent handoff for overloaded prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: When one agent's prompt mixes several tasks and gets confused, they split into separate agents per task (each possibly on a different LLM) and route between them via a system tool, keeping the same voice so the user doesn't notice the transfer.

takeaways.technique: Explicit tool timeouts with conversational filler
takeaways.what_they_do: Tool definitions carry a configurable timeout (max 120s); while waiting, the agent stays conversational and tells the user it is still looking up the response instead of going silent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent will actually like say, "Oh, I'm I'm currently looking that up in the system... we're still waiting kind of on the response."

takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend picking the LLM per use case, going down to small flash models when function-calling demands are light, and note function-calling reliability varies by model size.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can probably go down to like yeah a Gemini flash or flashlight um to like reduce the latency

takeaways.technique: RAG instead of stuffing the whole knowledge base
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that depending on the model you may not want the entire knowledge base in context, and enable retrieval as a mitigation for both context size and latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you might not want to put kind of the entire knowledge base into the context. So you can you can enable rack there
